key_results: Thickness-dependent crossover in Mn₃Sn: thin devices show intrinsic spin-orbit torque switching without Joule heating; thicker devices limited to ns timescales by heating
comments: Clarifies how engineering layer thickness suppresses thermal effects, revealing underlying picosecond spin dynamics of antiferromagnets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reducing layer thickness suppresses Joule heating and reveals intrinsic picosecond spin-orbit torque switching
hypotheses.result: Clear signature of intrinsic mechanism observed in thin devices; heating dominates thick devices

title: The impact of metastability on the high-pressure behavior of cerium
task: Resolve phase-selection mechanism in high-pressure cerium via kinetics vs. equilibrium
key_results: Compression pathway governs phase selection: slow RT compression→orthorhombic α′; slow/moderate low-T compression→monoclinic α″; γ phase metastably persists beyond expected stability field
comments: Large-volume neutron diffraction reveals kinetic path-dependence dominates equilibrium—microstructural memory governs Ce phase diagram at high pressure.

model_io.model: High-pressure Ce under controlled compression pathways

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phase selection in Ce governed by kinetics and microstructural memory, not equilibrium thermodynamics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: slow compression conditions and low-temperature pathways stabilize distinct phases; γ persists metastably

title: A macroscopic condensation theory for vibrational strong coupling effects
task: Explain vibrational strong coupling (VSC) effects via macroscopic condensation of vibrations
key_results: VSC-induced reaction-rate modifications and phase transitions explained by macroscopic vibrational condensate formation above critical Rabi splitting threshold
comments: Shifts focus from single-polariton physics to many-body condensation—potentially unifying explanation for diverse VSC phenomena.

model_io.model: Ensemble of molecules in optical microcavity

hypotheses.hypothesis: VSC effects arise from macroscopic condensation of vibrations above critical Rabi splitting
hypotheses.result: Theoretical framework developed explaining rate modifications and phase transitions

title: Fermionic parton theory of Rydberg $${{\mathbb{Z}}}_{2}$$Z2 quantum spin liquids
task: Identify Z₂ quantum spin liquid candidate in Rydberg-atom array on ruby lattice
key_results: Best-matching mean-field Ansatz identified via static structure-factor comparison with DMRG; detailed dynamical correlations provided for experimental validation
comments: Systematic symmetry-group framework applied to distinguish QSL candidates—valuable reference for programmable quantum simulators.

model_io.model: DMRG calculations + projective symmetry group analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ruby-lattice Rydberg array realizes topologically ordered Z₂ QSL
hypotheses.result: Candidate identified; structure-factor predictions match DMRG within tested ansatze

title: Atomic-scale mechanism of anisotropic ion migration in 2D Bi2O2Se nanodevices
task: Resolve atomic-scale mechanism of anisotropic ion migration in 2D Bi₂O₂Se memristors
key_results: Vertical vs. lateral fields enable distinct ion-migration pathways: vertical yields reversible ordered conductive D-Bi₂O₂Se (abrupt switching); lateral produces topotactic heterostructures with linear conductance modulation
comments: Elegant in situ TEM + DFT study directly visualizing structural evolution; crystallographic anisotropy governs switching mechanism and functionality.

model_io.model: DFT calculations of ion migration barriers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Anisotropic migration barriers for O²⁻/Se²⁻ ions create directionally dependent switching pathways
hypotheses.result: Vertical: reversible localized switching; lateral: smooth topotactic transformation confirmed via in situ TEM + DFT

title: Temporal self-similarity reveals percolation universality classes in complex networks
task: Characterize percolation universality classes in complex networks via temporal dynamics
key_results: Two independent Fisher critical exponents (τc, τs) uniquely determine universality class; real networks exhibit distinct classes from idealized models
comments: Clever use of temporal self-similarity to extract universal scaling relations from heterogeneous systems without explicit critical thresholds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Real-world networks follow universality classes distinct from canonical models due to higher-order structure
hypotheses.result: Validated across biological, social, and infrastructural networks

title: Ion-disrupted hydrogen-bond networks enable fast water transport under two-dimensional confinement
task: Elucidate role of ion-disrupted hydrogen-bond networks in confined-water transport
key_results: Weakly hydrated cations enhance water permeation by disrupting H-bond connectivity and increasing exchanging-hydration-water population; vermiculite-based channels show 55% faster transport with weak cations vs. strong
comments: Clever use of tunable interlayer cations to probe ion–water interaction effects; IR spectroscopy + MD simulations reveal H-bond restructuring mechanism.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Weakly hydrated cations disrupt H-bond networks, enhancing exchanging-water population and diffusion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: H-bond disruption correlates with faster water transport; IR and MD show shifted O-H stretch and increased hydration-water mobility

title: Kagome-Lattice Magnetic Catalysts: Electric Potential and Magnetic Field Dual Modulation for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Reaction
task: Optimize ORR catalysis in Kagome-lattice metal–organic frameworks via dual electric/magnetic modulation
key_results: FM Fe₃(CN₃)₂ achieves 2e⁻ ORR (0.03 V overpotential); temperature/potential switching to AFM state enables 4e⁻ pathway; magnetic field tunes relative stability of configurations
comments: DFT + Monte Carlo study leverages magnetic state tunability for catalytic control—complementary roles of electric potential and magnetic field clearly delineated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnetic-state switching via electric potential modulates ORR pathway from 2e⁻ to 4e⁻; external field tunes stability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via DFT and Monte Carlo for Fe₃(CN₃)₂ near room-temperature transitions

title: Unconventional skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets
task: Engineer unconventional skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnet via effective-field mechanism
key_results: Two skyrmion families in CoB/CoFeB synthetic antiferromagnet: conventional-polarity at large fields, inverse-polarity at small fields (field reversal); all textures reside in CoFeB driven by RKKY field from CoB
comments: Effective-field approach enables programmable 3D spin textures with layer-selected polarity—powerful control mechanism for skyrmion-based computing.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Asymmetric interlayer-exchange effects on sublattices create competing effective fields enabling inverse-polarity skyrmions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: two skyrmion families observed; RKKY mechanism confirmed via element-resolved X-ray magnetometry and correlative microscopies

title: Error correction of a logical qubit encoded in a single atomic ion
task: Demonstrate quantum error correction in single atomic ion using spin-cat logical states
key_results: Error reduction by factor of 2.2; qubit lifetime extension by factor up to 1.5; autonomous correction without mid-circuit ancilla measurements
comments: Innovative use of internal Hilbert-space structure to reduce qubit overhead; approach scalable to few-qubit devices like quantum network nodes.

model_io.model: Single atomic ion with multiple internal states

hypotheses.hypothesis: Autonomous error correction using spin-cat states reduces overhead vs. multi-qubit codes
hypotheses.result: 2.2× error reduction and 1.5× lifetime extension demonstrated

title: Emergence of phase coherence in a magnon Bose–Einstein condensate
task: Observe spontaneous phase coherence formation in magnon Bose–Einstein condensate
key_results: Direct observation of incoherent magnon gas thermalizing into coherent condensate with well-defined macroscopic phase; evidence of spontaneous symmetry breaking
comments: Phase-referenced detection technique enables tracking of global coherence acquisition—elegant experimental validation of core BEC prediction.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnon gas undergoes spontaneous phase formation upon BEC transition with well-defined macroscopic phase
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via phase-referenced detection tracking coherence emergence

title: Tutorial: a beginner’s guide to fast neutron detection with an EJ-309 detector
task: Develop accessible protocol for fast-neutron detection and quantification using EJ-309 scintillation detector
key_results: Comprehensive guide to detector configuration, calibration, and characterization in mixed neutron/gamma-ray fields; demonstrated on benchtop DD reactor
comments: Tutorial contribution democratizing neutron diagnostics methodology—addresses practical challenges limiting broader adoption in fusion research.

model_io.model: EJ-309 liquid organic scintillator detector + benchtop DD reactor

hypotheses.hypothesis: Systematic calibration and characterization protocol enables reliable fast-neutron detection in mixed fields
hypotheses.result: Methodology validated on benchtop reactor; accessible to broader scientific communities

title: Role of conducting filler on electromagnetic shielding performance of CaCu3Ti4O12/CoFe2O4/Al/silicone composites over wide frequency range
task: Optimize electromagnetic shielding performance via conducting-filler-enhanced ceramic/ferrite/silicone composites
key_results: CCAS-4 composite (CCTO/CFO/Al/silicone) achieves 12 dB shielding effectiveness (94% attenuation) over 8–22 GHz; enhancement driven by electrical conductivity, interfacial polarization, and magnetic properties
comments: Synergistic multi-phase design; Al conducting filler critical for high-frequency EMI attenuation in practical applications.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Synergistic combination of electrical conductivity, interfacial polarization, and magnetic response maximizes shielding effectiveness
hypotheses.result: CCAS-4 achieves 12 dB SET with 94% microwave attenuation

title: An artificial neural network with analytical self-attenuation correction for rapid efficiency calibration of HPGe detectors
task: Calibrate HPGe detector efficiency using neural network with analytical self-attenuation correction
key_results: Mean pipeline MAPE 2.7% (well-type) and 1.8% (XtRa detector) across 8 test materials; ray-tracing solid-angle correction superior to parallel-beam formula; <1 second prediction time vs. 10–100 s per MC simulation
comments: Hybrid ML-analytical approach elegantly decouples learning from domain-specific physics; ray-tracing correction essential for both detector geometries.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Solid-angle weighted ray-tracing geometric correction universally outperforms parallel-beam formula
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for both well-type and planar XtRa detectors across 8 materials (ρ=1.0–2.7 g cm⁻³)

title: A new ultra-high gain CI-based DC/DC converter with low voltage and current stresses
task: Design ultra-high-gain DC/DC converter with low component stresses
key_results: Quadratic voltage gain with three-winding coupled-inductor topology; 25 V→400 V (16× gain) at 200 W with <5% component stress reduction compared to standard topologies
comments: Engineering contribution combining coupled-inductor and voltage-multiplier designs; experimental validation on 200 W prototype demonstrates practical viability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Semi-trans-inverse secondary winding operation enables high gain at low turns ratio with minimal stress
hypotheses.result: Validated via steady-state analysis and 200 W prototype measurements

title: Exact solutions and instability analysis of a fifth-order nonlinear evolution equation exhibiting multi-scale wave structures
task: Construct exact traveling-wave solutions and assess stability of fifth-order nonlinear PDE
key_results: Multiple solution families derived via modified extended mapping method (bright/dark solitons, periodic, rational, elliptic-function, combined structures); dispersion relation characterizes instability regimes
comments: Systematic analytical approach yields unified family of solutions; linear stability framework identifies onset conditions for perturbation growth.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modified extended mapping method yields multiple solution classes in unified framework
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: solitons, periodic, singular, rational, and combined solutions derived systematically

hypotheses.hypothesis: Linear perturbation framework identifies parameter regimes with unstable wave evolution
hypotheses.result: Dispersion relation analysis determines instability onset conditions

title: Medium-adaptive wideband near-field antenna for microwave detection of internal cavities in plant stems
task: Design medium-adaptive wideband near-field antenna for cavity detection in plant stems
key_results: Compact quasi-planar dipole with dual-ring balun achieves wideband matching (2.0–3.0 GHz) in lossy wood tissue; mutual-coupling sensitivity optimal at 2.76 GHz for internal cavity detection
comments: Physics-based design incorporating realistic dielectric loading; clever use of mutual coupling between elements for cavity localization.

model_io.model: Medium-adaptive antenna in cylindrical wood medium

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mutual coupling between antenna elements provides strong sensitivity to internal cavities vs. reflection coefficient
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via sensitivity analysis; optimal frequency band identified at 2.76 GHz

title: Physicochemical properties and DFT insight into choline chloride-levulinic acid deep eutectic solvent and its binary mixtures with carboxylic acids
task: Characterize physicochemical and thermodynamic properties of choline chloride–levulinic acid DES and binary mixtures
key_results: Excess molar volumes, compressibilities, and refractive-index deviations quantified; DFT/NCI/RDG analysis reveals intermolecular interaction mechanisms; Lorentz-Lorenz model successfully predicts properties
comments: Comprehensive experimental + computational characterization; DES is promising green solvent but intermolecular interactions with carboxylic acids require careful modeling.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lorentz-Lorenz equation accurately models optical and volumetric properties across full composition range
hypotheses.result: Validated via experimental measurements

title: Dynamics of laser-induced optical switching in silicon and GaAs: impact of spatially resolved transport and density-dependent optical losses
task: Model time-resolved optical response of photoexcited semiconductors under nanosecond laser excitation
key_results: Spatially resolved diffusion-recombination model predicts reflectance/transmittance/absorptance for Si and GaAs; density-dependent Drude damping captures epsilon-near-zero enhancement
comments: Rigorous treatment of finite-geometry effects and depth-dependent carrier distribution essential—spatial averaging obscures density-dependent optical losses.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Density-dependent Drude relaxation rate correction is necessary for accurate optical response near epsilon-near-zero
hypotheses.result: Consistency with reflectance/transmittance measurements for Si and GaAs confirmed

title: Anomalous localization and mobility edges in non-Hermitian quasicrystals with disordered imaginary gauge fields
task: Study localization transitions in non-Hermitian quasicrystals with disorder
key_results: Anomalous mobility edge between two localized regimes (skin accumulation vs. Anderson localization); wave-packet dynamics show spectral-topology-driven drift averaged over disorder
comments: Novel mechanism where both sides of a mobility edge represent confinement rather than spreading, extending localization physics to open systems.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-Hermitian disorder creates anomalous mobility edge between two localized sectors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via Lyapunov exponents and spectral analysis

title: Nonlinear tripartite coupling of trapped electrons with magnons in a hybrid quantum system
task: Demonstrate nonlinear tripartite coupling in trapped-electron–magnon hybrid systems
key_results: Tunable strong spin-magnon-motion coupling enabled by electron zero-point motion; enables rapid few-body entangled-state preparation
comments: Leverages multiple degrees of freedom (motion and spin) of a single particle to mediate inter-particle coupling—a creative exploitation of available quantum resources.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Large spatial extent of electron zero-point motion enables strong tunable spin-magnon-motion coupling
hypotheses.result: Theoretical prediction consistent with trapped-ion and quantum-magnonics techniques
